rationale: Both offline devices are battery-powered SEN-D1 sensors that logged low-battery warnings (7% and 9%) immediately before going offline, with healthy RSSI (-58 to -63 dBm) and compatible firmware. The base station is online with a good uplink and all 5 other devices online, ruling out a base-station failure. The customer confirmed both sensors were installed on the same day ~14 months ago and never had batteries replaced, so they drained simultaneously — a coincidence, not a systemic fault.

repair_steps: Instruct the customer to replace the batteries in the Back Door and Back Window sensors with fresh CR123A batteries.
After battery replacement, ask the customer to press the tamper button on each sensor to force a reconnection.
Verify in the app that both sensors come back online and show battery level above 20%.
Advise the customer to set a reminder to replace sensor batteries every 12 months to avoid recurrence.
output.customer_reply: Thanks for your patience. We found both sensors had low batteries (7% and 9%) and went offline. Your base station is fine. Please replace the batteries in the Back Door and Back Window sensors with fresh CR123A batteries, then press the tamper button on each to reconnect. They should come back online within a minute. We recommend replacing sensor batteries yearly to avoid this. Let us know if you need further help.

Customer reported a CAM-S1 in a detached garage going offline several times a day. RSSI was -86 dBm; all other devices normal. Installing an RP-1 repeater solved it. Resolved at frontline.
